correctness.rationale: For n>1 strongly pseudoperfect, the complement of every complement-closed divisor representation has positive-or-zero mass A=sigma(n)-2n. Each omitted nonsquare orbit contributes d+n/d<=A, giving d^2-Ad+n<=0 and roots (A±sqrt(A^2-4n))/2 when A>=2sqrt(n); if A<2sqrt(n) no two-member orbit may be omitted. The square-root singleton is expressly excepted. When sigma(n)<=3n, A<=n<n+1, hence the (1,n) orbit is in every representation; Wang--Zelinsky Theorem 5 applies to any one such representation and proves strong pseudoperfectness of n^k for all integers k>=1. For n=720, sigma=2418, A=978 and the five omitted orbits (1,720),(10,72),(16,45),(18,40),(20,36) sum to 978 and are pairwise disjoint; the retained complement-closed divisor set sums to 1440. Independently implemented exact set-valued subset-sum DP over every integer 2<=n<720, removing distinguished orbit (1,n) and allowing each other complement orbit independently, gave zero escape candidates; an independent integer bitset DP agreed on each of 719 integers 2..720. Each orbit including square-root singleton is considered exactly once, so this proves the finite leastness claim. Neither the finite calculation nor the checker proves an unbounded power theorem; that step comes from cited Theorem 5.
risks: Theorem 5 is an external mathematical theorem, not re-proved in the assigned package; primary theorem statement and constructive proof inspected.
Finite cutoff is an exhaustive finite computation only through 719; no inference about larger n or absence of extremely-strong representations at n=720.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge qualified PASS applies to the natural representation-level least-escape boundary 720 in conjunction with the global abundance region. The omitted-mass bound and quadratic band are elementary observations already essentially present as the inequality used in Wang--Zelinsky Proposition 15; they are not credited as standalone major novelties. The sigma<=3n power consequence is likewise a short corollary of Theorem 5 plus the elementary mass bound. Nevertheless, the exact least n>1 admitting ANY strongly pseudoperfect representation with (1,n) omitted, including the five-orbit witness and exhaustive lower bound, is not stated or implied by the inspected primary text, known full published Resultary cases, or the OEIS entry; it identifies a natural sharp first failure of representation-wise forcing relevant to Theorem 5. No assertion is made that 720 lacks another representation containing (1,n), or that power closure fails at 720.
residual_risks: The core pair inequality and power corollary are cheap deductions from the published primary argument; positive originality depends materially on the exact natural 720 first-escape classification, not on repackaging Proposition 15.
Historical unpublished divisor-subset computations might record the same first escape without a searchable title; failed searching cannot certify novelty.
Some papers classify related constrained factor shapes or exactly one omitted pair; no exhaustive scan of every article or private database was possible.

value.rationale: The object is the standard complement-closed strong-pseudoperfect divisor representation; the distinguished (1,n) orbit is exactly Wang--Zelinsky Theorem 5’s hypothesis for power closure. The abundance threshold provides a clean structural region where that hypothesis holds for EVERY representation, and the independently verified first integer permitting its failure in some representation is precisely 720 with an explicit five-pair witness. The number 720 is not an arbitrary slice: it is a natural first boundary for an inclusion property singled out by the motivating open question. The exact cutoff serves as a small reproducible benchmark for studies of representation quantifiers and non-forced-pair phenomena. Standalone innovation in the one-line omitted-pair bound is modest and must not be overstated. No claim that 720 disproves extremely strong pseudoperfectness or power closure.
risks: The forced band and abundance corollary alone would be routine; value hinges on the motivated exact representation-level cutoff.
The first-escape example is a failure of every-representation forcing, not of existence of another good representation, which limits downstream conclusions.
